# Template: game_tree
An extensive-form game tree: the first mover at the root, actions as labeled branches, either payoff pairs "(a, b)" at the leaves or a second-mover node with its own branches (up to three levels, three actions per node), plus optional backward-induction solving that highlights each player's best reply and boxes the subgame-perfect outcome. Defaults to the classic entry game (Out, or In followed by Fight/Accommodate — the non-credible-threat lesson). Choose this scene for ANY request about sequential games, extensive form, game trees, backward induction, subgame-perfect equilibrium, credible or non-credible threats, or first-mover advantage.

Element ids your commands can reference:
- node_r: the root node (with its player number)
- node_<path>: an internal node, path = action indices from the root joined by _ (e.g. node_1)
- edge_<path>: the branch leading to that node/leaf, with its action label
- payoff_<path>: the payoff pair at a leaf, e.g. payoff_1_0
- legend: who is player 1 and 2 (a group)
- solution: the backward-induction marks — thick accent overlays on best replies plus a box around the equilibrium payoffs (a group, when solve)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw the entry game and solve it by backward induction." → params: {"solve":true,"title":"The entry game"}
Request: "Show a sequential game where the second mover's threat is not credible." → params: {"players":["Challenger","Champion"],"solve":true}

In YAML: `template: game_tree` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
